narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Today feels much like yesterday with about the same warmth and calmer winds, marking another wet day. Little has changed materially since this morning's forecast, though isolated convective showers and thunderstorms remain on track across the Nyanza Basin through late evening before clearing overnight.

## Today's Forecast
With the sun setting, daytime high temperatures reached 30°C / 86°F earlier this afternoon. For the rest of tonight, temperatures will cool steadily to an overnight low of 19°C / 66°F. Isolated convective showers and thunderstorms remain possible through 21:00 EAT, bringing potential rainfall totals between 0.4 mm (0.02 in) and 3.5 mm (0.14 in). Recent surface observations from Kisumu Airport confirm Cumulonimbus activity in the area with light easterly winds at 22 km/h (12 kt). Winds through the late evening will calm to 7 km/h (4 kt) to 11 km/h (6 kt) from the E/NE. Ground air quality sensors at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue, and Dunga Beach are currently stale (4 hours old); reliance on CAMS model guidance indicates Moderate air quality (US AQI 93–97, PM2.5 around 37–43 µg/m³).

## Extended Outlook
Monday (August 24) will see continued wet conditions with daytime highs around 30°C / 86°F and evening rain totals of 3.8 mm (0.15 in) to 9.2 mm (0.36 in). A transition toward drier, warmer weather begins Tuesday (August 25) and Wednesday (August 26) as rain probabilities drop below 30% and afternoon highs rise to 31°C / 88°F to 32°C / 90°F. From Thursday (August 27) through Sunday (August 30), high confidence guidance across ECMWF and GFS points to dry, sunny weather with daytime highs reaching 33°C / 91°F to 34°C / 93°F and lows around 17°C / 63°F to 19°C / 66°F.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Atmospheric instability remains elevated through mid-evening, with CAPE model spread ranging from 90 J/kg (GFS) to 900 J/kg (ECMWF) and 1530 J/kg (UKMO). Localized thunderstorms, frequent lightning, and short-lived wind gusts up to 30 km/h (16 kt) remain a hazard for Kisumu Central and surrounding lowlands until 21:00 EAT before convective activity tapers off.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Over open water on eastern Lake Victoria, evening winds from the W/SW at 11 km/h (6 kt) with gusts up to 26 km/h (14 kt) will shift E/NE overnight. Elevated CAPE values over the lake tonight (1380–1570 J/kg ECMWF, 1850–2340 J/kg UKMO) present a risk for nocturnal and early morning thunderstorms. Tomorrow morning brings renewed shower activity with NE winds strengthening to 22 km/h (12 kt) and gusts up to 30 km/h (16 kt).

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1006 hPa) and highest toward the south (1020 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the north, northwest, southwest, and west, while pressure overhead is falling. Nyanza Basin regional MSLP averages 1015.5 hPa today and is projected to deepen to 1012–1013 hPa over the next 48 to 72 hours, maintaining low-level moisture convergence into the basin.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Evaluating today's updates against the 12-check verification track record, Best Match (83% skill) and ICON (75% skill) maintain superior Day+0 rain performance relative to GFS (50% skill). Kenya Met holds a 33% rain verification rate across 3 checks and aligns with numerical consensus for a wet transition today into Monday. Model biases remain consistent: GFS and ECMWF systematically under-forecast peak surface winds by 11 to 20 km/h, while ICON retains a nocturnal cold bias (-2.3°C) and UKMO a nocturnal warm bias (+1.4°C). ECMWF is heavily weighted for the Day+3 transition due to its 89% verification skill at that lead time.

morning_issuance.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Today feels much like yesterday with about the same warmth and calmer winds, marking another wet day. Warm afternoon temperatures will precede evening cloud buildup and isolated convective showers.

## Today's Forecast
Conditions across Kisumu Central and the surrounding Nyanza lowlands will start dry with sunny intervals through mid-morning. Daytime maximum temperatures will reach 30°C / 86°F around 15:00 EAT before cloud cover increases rapidly. Solar radiation will peak around midday with a Very High UV Index of 9.1. Winds will build from the SW at 15 km/h (8 kt) during the early afternoon, generating peak gusts near 36 km/h (19 kt). Precipitation chances rise significantly between 16:00 and 19:00 EAT as atmospheric instability develops, with rainfall totals forecast between 1.1 mm (0.04 in) and 5.6 mm (0.22 in). Overnight minimum temperatures will drop to 19°C / 66°F under partial cloud cover. Ground AQI sensors at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue, and Dunga Beach are currently stale (4 hours old), so air quality assessment relies on CAMS model guidance, indicating Moderate conditions (US AQI 86-95, PM2.5 peaking at 39.7 µg/m³).

## Extended Outlook
Monday (August 24) will remain wet with elevated rain probability across ECMWF and GFS, bringing 3.0 mm to 8.4 mm of precipitation and high temperatures around 30°C / 86°F. A notable drying and warming trend begins Tuesday (August 25) and Wednesday (August 26), as daytime highs rise to 31°C / 88°F and precipitation chances drop below 30%. From Thursday (August 27) through Sunday (August 30), stable extended guidance from ECMWF and GFS points to dry, sunny conditions with daytime temperatures reaching 33°C / 91°F to 34°C / 93°F and overnight lows near 17°C / 63°F to 19°C / 66°F.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) will rise significantly late this afternoon, ranging from 630 J/kg in GFS and 950 J/kg in ECMWF up to an extreme 4140 J/kg in UKMO around 18:00 EAT. This instability supports localized thunderstorm activity across the Nyanza Basin. Thunder without significant localized rainfall remains a distinct possibility due to lake-breeze convergence dynamics. Gusty, erratic winds up to 36 km/h (19 kt) may accompany thunderstorm onset.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Open water conditions over eastern Lake Victoria will experience early morning and mid-day rain showers (10.2 mm to 14.6 mm total precipitation expected between 04:00 and 12:00 EAT). CAPE values over the lake remain high overnight and into the morning (1600 J/kg to 2250 J/kg in ECMWF, 2500 J/kg to 3080 J/kg in UKMO), creating storm hazards for morning lake transport. Winds over open water will reach 31.5 km/h (17 kt) with gusts up to 30 km/h (16 kt) from the NE/E during the morning, shifting to W/NW at 15 km/h (8 kt) by mid-afternoon.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1005 hPa) and highest toward the south (1019 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the north, northwest, southwest, and west, while pressure overhead is falling. Regionally across the Nyanza Basin points, MSLP averages 1015.5 hPa today and is projected to deepen to 1012-1014 hPa over the next 48 to 72 hours. This gradual pressure fall enhances low-level moisture convergence from Lake Victoria, fueling late afternoon and evening convection.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Long-run review findings across 12 verified days show Best Match as the leading Day+0 rain caller (83% accuracy) and GFS as the weakest (50% accuracy). Systematic model biases include GFS, ECMWF, ICON, and UKMO consistently under-forecasting peak wind speeds by 9 to 20 km/h. ICON exhibits a persistent nocturnal cold bias (-2.3°C error), whereas UKMO exhibits a nocturnal warm bias (+1.4°C error). Given ECMWF's strong Day+3 rain verification skill (89%) and consistent performance on onset timing, higher weight is assigned to ECMWF for today's rain window (16:00-19:00 EAT) and the extended forecast transition.
